split_note: StrategyQA test.json has no answer labels. We use a held-out 10% of the 2061-problem train split (207 problems), capped at 200 for evaluation. Both baseline and TAPR runs use RANDOM_SEED=42, so both see the identical eval set.
provenance: exact — transcribed from Colab run logs

experiment_1_trained_on_strategyqa.description: Models trained directly on StrategyQA (1854 train problems, 400 steps).
experiment_1_trained_on_strategyqa.interpretation: The 1.0pp TAPR-vs-baseline gap is well within the 3.4pp standard error at n=200. Cannot claim TAPR > baseline from this experiment alone.

experiment_2_cross_task_transfer.description: GSM8K-trained models evaluated on StrategyQA. Neither model saw any StrategyQA data during training. THIS IS THE KEY RESULT.

interpretation.headline: Outcome-only GRPO on GSM8K degraded StrategyQA performance by 5.5pp below the untrained model. TAPR degraded it by only 1.0pp.
interpretation.mechanism_hypothesis: ORM optimizes for format compliance (numbered steps ending in ####), causing catastrophic over-specialization. TAPR optimizes for step-to-step logical validity, a more transferable property.
interpretation.open_question: Two competing explanations: (A) TAPR is an implicit regularizer that simply moves the policy less; (B) TAPR moves the policy a comparable amount but in a different direction. Distinguishing A from B requires the policy drift experiment (see ROADMAP.md).
interpretation.caveat: Single seed. Multi-seed replication is the top-priority next experiment.

reward_degeneracy.definition: Fraction of training groups where all G=4 rollouts received identical rewards, yielding zero advantage and zero gradient.
reward_degeneracy.note: StrategyQA baseline degeneracy (~0.625) exceeds GSM8K baseline degeneracy (~0.525). Hypothesis: on a binary yes/no task, an uncertain model tends to emit the same answer across all rollouts, collapsing reward variance more often than on numeric-answer tasks.
